diffs.diff: maximum supply: part 5.5 V, datasheet reading 3.6 V
diffs.evidence: The model is the ProtoCentral MAX30205 breakout, whose VIN pin feeds an on-board AP2112K-3.3V LDO (schematic pc_max30205_brk.sch: V_REG_LDO value "AP2112K-3.3V", plus 3x BSS138 level shifters); the chip itself only sees 3.3 V. ProtoCentral README Hardware Setup: "Vin / 5V | Vin (3.3V also supported, change the solder jumper on the back; default is 5V) | Power supply". The AP2112K accepts up to 6 V input, so a 5.5 V VIN maximum is valid. The second reading's 3.6 V is the bare chip's VDD limit (MAX30205 datasheet: Operating Supply Voltage VDD 2.7-3.3 V; absolute max VDD -0.3 V to +4 V), which applies to the IC, not the breakout's VIN pin.
